items.summary: On Nov 5, Airbnb raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast from “at least mid-teens” to the “high teens”, citing resilient global leisure travel demand. Shares rose 11% in extended trading. The company also authorised a US$12 billion repurchase programme and expects an AI agent roll-out in the first half of 2027, while CFO Ellie Mertz said unrest in Europe and conflict in the Middle East are not expected to materially impact its current quarter.
items.title: Airbnb Raises Full-Year Revenue Growth Forecast on Strong Travel Demand

items.summary:
Asia’s tech-heavy markets fell sharply on Nov 6, deepening after a rout in US stocks that marked the steepest drop since April. Japan’s Nikkei slumped 7%, while South Korea and Taiwan benchmarks dropped more than 8%. The KOSPI plunge triggered circuit breakers halting trade for 20 minutes. Around $3 trillion was wiped off S&P 500 companies, with investors worried Democrats may curb the AI boom. Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell nearly 10% and 12%, while SoftBank Group slid 11%. Some analysts called the selloff overdone, though others warned of forced liquidations. Meanwhile, bonds rose as investors sought refuge in safe assets.

visual null}},{
items.title: Asian Markets Plunge Amid AI Selloff and Regulatory Fears

items.summary: A Singaporean forum post by Raymond Lim argues that petrol motorcycles remain among the most noisy vehicles, especially at night and in carparks. The author notes strong progress under the Green Plan but says motorcycles have been left behind. He urges authorities to give electric motorcycles a more prominent role through incentives, charging or battery-swopping infrastructure, firm enforcement against loud or modified bikes, and technology to identify repeat offenders.
items.title: Singapore forum calls for electric motorcycle push against noise pollution

items.summary: Palo Alto Networks is reportedly in talks to acquire Clutch Security, a startup securing AI agents' access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus milestone-based payouts. The Information first reported the discussions. Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million and now approaches $10 million ARR, implying about 50 times its revenue. Both companies declined comment.
items.title: Palo Alto Networks in Talks to Acquire AI Agent Security Startup Clutch

items.summary: Elon Musk has openly hoped to make SpaceX a competitor to Verizon and AT&T in mobile services, but Democrats’ strong showing in the 2026 midterms complicates that goal. Over the past month SpaceX bought an 800 MHz spectrum portfolio from Grain Management and struck a deal with Qualcomm for base stations. Lawmakers plan investigations into conflicts of interest, Musk’s federal contracts, his role regarding Ukraine’s internet access, and DOGE data handling.
items.title: Midterm Blue Wave Threatens SpaceX Mobile Plans

items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Small, the first model of its second Inkling generation and a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) with 594B total and 17B active parameters. It accepts text and image input and supports variable reasoning effort but does not support audio as of now. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index it scores 31, up from 13 for its predecessor Inkling Small, ranking #4 of 29 in its price class. It scored 86. 3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 (Hard) and 13. 1% on Terminal-Bench 4. 0. Weights are closed at launch, with an Apache 2. 0 release planned after external safety testing and red-teaming. The model is live on Tinker for fine-tuning and inference. All scores come from the lab's benchmark table run at effort 0. 99 (xhigh) and temperature 1. 0; most rows use third-party evaluators such as Artificial Analysis, Scale AI and Vals. Prices are $0. 30 per 1M input tokens and $1.
items.title: Thinking Machines Lab Releases Multimodal MoE Model Inkling 2 Small

items.summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission approved a ₹3.46 per unit tariff for procuring 10 MW of grid-connected solar power from Agrowin Agri Solutions Private Limited, effective under a November 4, 2026 order enabling a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement. Agrowin won an e-reverse auction on September 26, 2025, beating Wisdom Agricare’s ₹3.56 bid for 1 MW. The procurement supports Bihar meeting its Renewable Purchase Obligations through FY 2029–30; the Commission directed petitioners to complete technical and legal amendments before finalizing the agreement.
items.title: BERC Approves Tariff for Bihar Solar Procurement

items.summary: Crude oil prices were heading for a sharp weekly decline as Brent crude and WTI shed 12% since Monday, driven by hopes that the Middle East war could end quickly after U.S. midterm results. At writing, Brent traded at $99.42 per barrel and WTI at $91.242, both up from Thursday’s close on reports of fresh tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warn prices may stay supported but remain volatile amid uncertainty over escalation between the United States and Iran.
items.title: Oil Prices Face Weekly Drop Amid Tanker Attacks and Peace Hopes

items.summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission directed the Bihar State Power Generation Company Limited to submit corrected tender documents for a proposed 150 MW solar project with a 300 MWh battery storage system in Bihar. The direction followed an October 12 hearing that found deficiencies, and BSPGCL had not yet filed updated versions of its Request for Selection document and draft power purchase agreement incorporating agreed modifications. BERC set November 9 as the deadline; the next hearing is scheduled for November 12 at 11:30 AM to consider the matter further.
items.title: BERC Orders BSPGCL To Fix Solar Tender Documents

items.summary: US lawmakers summoned Nvidia's Jensen Huang to brief Congress privately over alleged ties between him and Alice Huang, accused of passing information about Nvidia's chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairs reportedly want answers, citing reports that the two shared a close relationship. Intelligence officials in at least three countries suspected Alice Huang was sharing Nvidia technology with Chinese intelligence.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Summoned by US Lawmakers Over Alleged Chinese Espionage Links

items.summary: A report says Google is shortening the time deleted photos and videos stay in Trash from 60 days to 30. Users must recover items before deletion, or they may be lost permanently.
items.title: Google Photos Cuts Trash Recovery Window To 30 Days

items.summary: Santiago Peña, Paraguay's rightwing president, resigned on Thursday after a banking crisis collapsed the country's financial system in recent days. At its centre was Ueno Bank, which under Peña grew from an obscure digital bank into one of the nation's largest lenders, claiming about 60% of adult customers. On Monday the central bank ordered Ueno into resolution over insolvency, freezing deposits for roughly 3 million people and leaving many without money for daily needs. Executives were arrested amid massive protests. Lawmakers voted unanimously to launch impeachment proceedings alleging misconduct tied to Peña's shareholding links. In a video he announced his resignation while pledging that the return of frozen funds would be guaranteed; opposition figures called it "the biggest fraud carried out from political power in the democratic era."
items.title: Paraguay's President Resigns After Banking Collapse

items.summary: Sheila Williams, from Golden Cross in East Sussex, says she has taken a winter waitress job to cover her heating oil costs. She reports her bill doubled since the start of 2026. A government spokesperson said £53m is pledged for vulnerable households and that the 4% tariff on home heating oil was removed. Rye Oil director Jon Reardon says prices have doubled since the war in the Middle East, affecting sales across south-east England.
items.title: Sussex Homeowner Takes Extra Job as Heating Oil Prices Soar

items.summary: An energy minister asked Great Britain’s largest suppliers to help households manage unpaid bills before the government spends almost £2.5bn to write off record debts of about 2.4m hardest-hit homes, part of a “circuit-breaker” strategy from last month’s budget that could save families about £130 over ten years. Attendees called it ambitious but stressed suppliers must not lose incentive to innovate while protecting households from future debt.
items.title: Energy Minister Urges Suppliers on Unpaid Bills Before Debt Write-off

items.summary: Ukraine's largest telecom operator, Kyivstar, raised its yearly revenue guidance after reporting third quarter revenue up 17.5 per cent year on year to $349 million (15.82 billion hryvnias). The company announced the change alongside its quarterly results.
items.title: Kyivstar Raises Annual Revenue Guidance on Strong Q3 Results

items.summary: In an Indian court on Friday, X said takedown notices it received were fake and not issued by Delhi Police. The Internet Freedom Foundation and SFLC.in had earlier told the platform that a purported police notice asked them to remove their accounts over accusations of defaming a Hindu nationalist group linked to India's ruling party.
items.title: X Says Takedown Notices Targeting Indian Free-Speech Groups Were Fake

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is urging businesses to publish salaries in job adverts now, rather than wait for compulsory legislation planned as soon as possible. The government argues the move helps first-time applicants and could prevent pay discrimination, following a consultation where 94% backed greater transparency. It follows an EHRC call for salary information access, amid falling disclosure rates on Adzuna (51%) and CIPD concerns over complex pay-setting.
items.title: Burnham urges firms to list pay in adverts ahead of new law

items.summary: About 600,000 of Nvidia's advanced AI chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to China, two people familiar with the matter said. The stockpile reflects Beijing's reluctance to increase reliance on US technology despite surging domestic demand from firms such as Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent. Chinese buyers have turned to intermediaries, pushing prices sharply higher.
items.title: Nvidia Chips Pile Up in Hong Kong Amid China Import Hold

items.summary: The Chinese Ministry of Commerce said China remains open to expanding US agricultural imports, but only if a $30-billion reciprocal tariff reduction is implemented. Spokesperson Huang Ling stated at a press conference that the arrangement would lower tariffs on about 90% of covered products and urged joint action to cut non-tariff barriers.
items.title: China Ties Farm Import Expansion to Tariff Cuts

items.summary: Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and Canadian trade minister Maninder Sidhu co-chaired the first ministerial-level meeting under China’s Joint Economic and Trade Commission mechanism in Beijing on November 3, 2026. The two sides discussed bilateral economic relations, traditional sectors such as oil and gas and agricultural products, and new areas including clean energy and smart agriculture. Both ministers described progress and called for continued cooperation; the parties signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a business leaders’ roundtable, according to China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM). This was the 29th meeting of the commission.
items.title: China and Canada Open First Ministerial Trade Talks

items.summary: Shanghai welcomed the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), which officials describe as reflecting China's ongoing commitment to opening up and sharing market opportunities globally. The event is framed around rising import demand and more diverse consumer preferences. Correspondent Cao Chufeng examines why global businesses continue to see commercial opportunity in China, presenting these observations without citing specific figures or independent verification.
items.title: Shanghai Hosts Ninth China International Import Expo, Signals Continued Opening Up

items.summary: Several European airlines were targeted with bomb threats on Thursday, Nov. 5, disrupting flights and alarming travelers across the region. Similar threats had occurred earlier in the week, adding to airspace and security anxiety. The item offers no figures beyond noting that five related items appear elsewhere in its source page.
items.title: Bomb Threats Divert Flights Across Europe

items.summary: Eva Geller, aged 90, died in hospital almost 12 months after being shot during the Bondi beach terror attack on 14 December. A senior Jewish community source said she had been hospitalized for injuries and later developed an infection before dying from a stroke. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called her death heartbreaking, saying her life was changed forever by antisemitism.
items.title: Bondi shooting victim Eva Geller dies a year after massacre

items.summary: A poll for AP and a news consortium found that 56% of surveyed voters said data centres were a crucial or major factor in their vote, while 76% would oppose building one locally. Opposition was stronger among Democratic voters but trailed government corruption (90%) and the cost of living (89%). BBC Verify notes it cannot say how many votes or seats opposition delivered, though three flipped states—Texas, Ohio and Iowa—all elected Democrats who proposed tighter data centre regulation. Meanwhile, spending on building data centres in August 2026 was $5bn (£4.2bn), five times the 2023 level.
items.title: Data centre opposition may have shaped US midterms, BBC Verify finds

items.summary: Relatives of Britons and other foreigners killed in July's Bédar fire say they are disgusted after regional politicians blocked an official inquiry, arguing the criminal investigation will not examine how people were warned. Nine British nationals died among 15 total; Sanz said no mobile alert was sent because it could not be tailored to communities. Families reject that and demand bells, police warnings and a public probe. Verdonckt says victims received only minutes of contact before flames arrived. The families have set up support groups and an appeal aiming to raise €100,000 (£83,000), collecting about €11,000 so far.
items.title: Grieving families demand inquiry into Spain wildfire deaths

items.summary: A Mongabay report frames extreme heat as an occupational crisis for the country's roughly 4.2 million garment workers, citing a World Bank finding that maximum temperatures rose about 1.1°C since 1980 and Dhaka's record April 2023 reading of 40.6°C. A 2025 study found peak indoor factory temperatures exceed 35°C on 37% of monitored days, while workers report collapses, dehydration and needle injuries; Aaron Bach notes clinics lack chronic-condition screening, and Cara Schulte says labor-rights gaps amplify risk.
items.title: Rising heat turns Bangladesh's garment floors into a health hazard

items.summary: Analysts said Thursday that a Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections could open new avenues for aid to Ukraine amid its war with Russia, while also raising scrutiny of President Trump's policies toward Moscow. Carrie Lee of the German Marshall Fund noted that the newly elected Congress provides a floor against delays or cuts to support.
items.title: Analysts See Midterm Gains Opening Doors for Ukraine Aid

items.summary: Tokyo marks one year since Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's remarks about possible Japanese military intervention in a Taiwan crisis triggered a diplomatic rupture with Beijing. The dispute began after her November 7, 2025 comments suggesting Self-Defense Forces deployment under collective self-defense rights in worst-case scenarios like a Chinese naval blockade. Relations show few signs of thawing as the two sides remain at odds.
items.title: Japan-China Tensions Persist One Year After Taiwan Remarks

items.summary: Fans of anime such as Love Live! Sunshine!! are visiting towns across Japan, bringing new opportunities to communities grappling with depopulation. In Numazu, Shizuoka Prefecture, the series drew seven fans known as 'Livers' who relocated to work at Awashima Hotel and elsewhere. Mayor Shuichi Yorishige said the city's population has fallen from a peak of 210,000 to 180,000, while pop culture tourism helps attract workers. Elsewhere, railway operators promote attractions along their networks, and in Kumamoto Prefecture statues of One Piece characters support recovery after earthquakes that killed more than 200 people. Still, many visitors only photograph locations without engaging the community, leaving towns to find ways to turn visits into lasting opportunities.
items.title: Anime Tourism Draws Fans and Workers to Japan's Shrinking Towns

items.summary: Andrew Dean Robson, 35, was sentenced to seven years in jail after crashing head-on into pregnant learner driver Angel Fewster on February 21, 2025. She was 27 weeks pregnant when her baby, Casey, was born by emergency caesarean with brain damage and died three days later. Robson tested positive for methylamphetamine; he pleaded guilty to dangerous driving occasioning death and drug driving. He will be eligible for parole in October 2029.
items.title: Drug driver jailed for crash that killed a premature baby

items.summary: Alleged kitchen knife murderer Conor O'Neill, 40, has been denied bail after being charged with murder following the death of his partner. He is alleged to have stabbed her twice while driving in Palmerston, near Darwin. The case returns to court next month, where his lawyer says he will likely argue 'defensive conduct' at trial.
items.title: Conor O'Neill denied bail over partner's death

items.summary: As Türkiye prepares to host COP31 in Antalya, critics describe its climate targets and policies as critically insufficient. The country remains heavily reliant on coal, which accounted for 33 per cent of electricity generation last year, while solar and wind together reached nearly 23 per cent. Türkiye operates one of Europe's largest solar farms at Karapınar, but advocates say it lacks a roadmap to phase out fossil fuels, including gas. Total greenhouse gas emissions in 2024 reached 584.5 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Duygu Kutluay of Beyond Fossil Fuels warned the plans are not compatible with Türkiye's net-zero target by 2053.
items.title: COP31 Host Türkiye Faces Criticism Over Coal Reliance Ahead of Climate Summit

items.summary: On November 6th, 2026, Euronews aired its morning news bulletin, presenting a round-up of the most important stories from around Europe and beyond. The newsroom described it as delivering latest and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel within just a few minutes, framed with what it called independence and a European perspective.
items.title: Euronews Broadcasts Morning News Roundup Across Europe and Beyond

items.summary: For the first time, a refugee team competed at the Youth Olympics in Senegal. Created by the International Olympic Committee and managed by the Olympic Refuge Foundation, the athletes came from camps in Kenya and Uganda to compete in judo, taekwondo and track and field. Sprinter Florence Masumbe said she was proud to represent her country.
items.title: Refugee Team Competes at Senegal's First Youth Olympics

items.summary: A Friday news roundup covers several developments, led by US President Donald Trump warning he may “destroy the rest” of Iran. The piece also reports Türkiye’s parliament approving a trilateral defense pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia (279 votes to 119), Israel's president Isaac Herzog saying government formation remains uncertain after consultations backing Gadi Eisenkot over Benjamin Netanyahu, Cristiano Ronaldo announcing his international retirement following November matches while continuing at Al Nassr, Harry Kane extending his Bayern Munich contract until June 30, 2029, Celtic beating Besiktas 3-2 in the Europa League, and US stock markets suffering their deepest one-day drop in 19 months as the Dow fell 1,834.84 points (3.44%) to 51,521.28.
items.title: Markets Plunge as Trump Threatens Iran and Ronaldo Announces Retirement

items.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Thursday he is working to recast the stalled UK-Mauritius deal on the Chagos Islands so it better addresses US concerns over the Diego Garcia military base. The original 2025 treaty, signed under Keir Starmer, would have transferred sovereignty to Mauritius while leasing the base for 99 years; Britain was set to pay £165 million ($222 million) annually for three years, then £120 million thereafter. The pact remains unratified after President Donald Trump rejected it as “terrible” and “ridiculous,” putting implementation legislation on hold.
items.title: Burnham Seeks Revised Chagos Agreement Amid US Pressure

items.summary: On a session marked by an AI-linked selloff, Indian IT stocks rose up to 3%, with TCS gaining to Rs 2,565 per share. The move followed plunges in US tech after Democrats won control of the Congress and fears that tougher AI regulation could slow infrastructure buildout. Nasdaq fell 6%—its worst drop since March 2020—and the selloff wiped off $3 trillion from S&P 500 companies. Analysts see Indian IT benefiting as the AI frenzy fades, though warnings persist: Michael Burry calls the market in a 'denial' mood lasting six to nine months, and Ashwath Damodaran says an AI bubble is coming with no way out.
items.title: Indian IT stocks rise as US AI rout deepens

items.summary: OpenAI released a National Community Compact pledging no nondisclosure agreements in data center deals, free electricity costs for residents, and public reporting on progress. The framework follows Thursday’s US elections where voters backed candidates supporting AI curbs; at least 45 projects worth $68 billion were disrupted by local opposition in the second quarter of 2026 per Data Center Watch. Chris Lehane noted some OpenAI projects may be delayed as communities respond to voter sentiment.
items.title: OpenAI Unveils Community Compact for Data Center Expansion

items.summary: Elon Musk removed pro-Republican posts from his X profile, including a pinned message urging voters to elect Republican senators and an Election Day post reading "Vote red today!". The deletions followed Democrat James Talarico's victory over Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race. His chatbot Grok confirmed removing the message after results showed major Republican losses.
items.title: Musk Deletes Pro-Republican Election Posts After Texas Losses

items.summary: Potential investors are raising doubts about whether Anthropic can proceed with its planned IPO roadshow next week in time for a November listing, four people familiar with investor discussions told Reuters. Investors want a more attractive valuation than the $1.5 trillion figure some had discussed, and may demand a larger discount to commit capital. The skepticism follows the sharpest technology stocks selloff in a year after Tuesday's US midterm elections. Anthropic declined to comment on the doubts. Analysts remain divided; one partner said such companies will still go public, while another described tech selling as uncomfortable but not abnormal, noting valuations have pulled back from long private-market gains.
items.title: Investors Question Anthropic's IPO Timing Amid AI Sell-Off

items.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the recent US midterm election results would have little impact on India-US relations. He asserted that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. Tharoor explained that while Congress controls budgetary matters and government spending, the President enjoys broad discretion in foreign affairs.
items.title: Tharoor Says Trump Keeps Foreign Policy Power After US Midterm Losses

items.summary: Perplexity has launched Teammates, a set of always-on AI agents designed to own ongoing work and compete with OpenAI's Dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet. Each agent carries a role, brief and rules for user involvement, drawing on projects from Perplexity Computer. CEO Aravind Srinivas said organisations may eventually run hundreds per person. Teammates are available now for Max subscribers at $200 a month.
items.title: Perplexity Launches Teammates AI Agents for Work

items.summary: Haseena Nishad, Managing Director of UAE-based World Star Holding, gifted foldable iPhone Duo phones to female employees at her company and shared the moment on Instagram. She called working with them one of the most rewarding parts of her leadership journey and described the gift as small but heartfelt. The company has a pattern of publicly rewarding staff: Khaleej Times reported Nishad gave iPhone 18s to 12 best performers, and Ynet reported that in 2024 it gifted 16 employees hotel stays.
items.title: Businesswoman Gifts Foldable iPhones To Female Employees

items.summary: Actor Prakash Raj called for a peaceful anti–Special Intensive Revision (SIR) protest in Kochi on Saturday, November 7. He urged students, young people, civil society members and representatives of various organisations to join the demonstration to 'save our democracy.' Criticising the government and Election Commission, he said, 'We will not tolerate killing democracy,' adding that citizens must come together and raise their voice.
items.title: Prakash Raj Urges Anti-SIR Protest in Kochi on Saturday

items.summary: India has begun releasing captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the wild to revive the critically-endangered species, but one of the first four birds released in Rajasthan was predated within days. Although the captive-breeding programme reports high survival rates, post-release survival is expected at around 30%. Wildlife Institute of India's Sutirtha Dutta says mortality from predation and starvation is anticipated during rewilding. The project has faced criticism over transparency and predator management. Forest officials suspect a wild GIB chick was predated earlier this year in Gujarat.
items.title: India's Great Indian Bustard Rewilding Faces Early Predation Losses Despite Progress

items.summary: Days after Republicans suffered a midterm election setback, media reports suggested Secretary of State Marco Rubio was weighing leaving the Trump administration as he considered his next moves. A Bloomberg report cited people familiar with the matter and said Rubio had not decided whether to step down from his roles as top diplomat and national security adviser, with no timetable set. The White House declined to comment on speculation, while the State Department denied any resignation consideration. Dylan Johnson called the reports 'complete and total fake news based on the word of anonymous sources.' Rubio dismissed them, saying working for Trump until the end of his term had always been his plan. Reports also mention possible 2028 presidential ambitions and VP JD Vance as succession contenders.
items.title: Rubio Weighs Departure After Republican Midterm Setback

items.summary: Hepatologist Dr Cyriac Abby Philips, known on X as 'The Liver Doc', lambasted Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal after the latter defended his Temple fitness device priced at ₹85,000. Philips called Temple a "scam," questioning its claims to measure brain blood flow and entropy, which he said rest on unproven science and poor methodology. He accused Goyal of defrauding customers under vague reassurances about spending millions for them. In response, Goyal posted seven points arguing that Temple is a fitness/wellness tracker outside medical purview, citing 14-day returns, $30m spent building it ($20m his own money), and upcoming pre-prints as evidence the product works.
items.title: Liver Doc attacks Goyal over ₹85,000 Temple device as scam

items.summary: Legal notices sent to Internet Freedom Foundation and Software Freedom Law Centre, purporting to come from the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and later backed by a Delhi Police “illegal content report,” turned out to be fabricated. An advisor Kanchan Gupta and RSS member Ratan Sharda denied on X that any such notices were sent; an anonymous police official told Scroll both documents are fake, noting the email address was likely created at 3.57 pm on October 29, 2026 – just six hours before it was used. The notice’s address traced to a different organisation registered in Nainital, and X later confirmed the notices came from an imposter while filing its own complaint.
items.title: Fake RSS and Delhi Police notices expose as hoax

items.summary: The Delhi Police arrested three contractors—Siraj, Tajuddin and Furkan—in connection with the collapse of a building under construction in Old Delhi’s Chawri Bazar that killed two persons. They were booked for culpable homicide not amounting to murder after police flagged unauthorised construction at the site five months earlier. The Municipal Corporation acknowledged an April warning about structural safety, alleging the owner used repairs as cover for new work. At least five remain feared trapped under debris.
items.title: Delhi Police Arrest Three Contractors Over Chawri Bazar Building Collapse

items.summary: During a hearing on Delhi's air quality, the Supreme Court identified the tradition of exchanging Diwali gifts as a contributor to vehicular pollution. The court made the remark while noting that the national capital continued to experience poor air conditions at the time.
items.title: Supreme Court Links Diwali Gift Culture to Delhi Air Pollution

items.summary: Parvinder Singh Jhota's family agreed to a post-mortem and ended its 22-day protest after talks with Punjab government representatives. The settlement followed the release of two arrested protesters on Thursday evening. The state accepted compensation of Rs 2 crore for the family, a job for his wife, a trauma centre in Jhota's memory, compensation for four injured people, and a memorial statue. Jhota was shot dead inside a medical store in Mansa on October 13 while hosting a Facebook Live session. His father Bhim Singh said last rites would be held Friday or Saturday after the family returns to Mansa with the body.
items.title: Jhota Family Agrees Post-Mortem, Ends Punjab Protest

items.summary: Nashra Naim became the first woman vice-president of Aligarh Muslim University's students' union, which celebrates a 105-year history. Women candidates won six of 13 posts; Naim secured 7,091 votes against her nearest rival's 5,818. The elections followed an eight-year gap amid student protests and were declared by Prof Javaid Talib and Prof Nazia Hasan on Friday.
items.title: AMU Students' Union Elects First Woman Vice-President in Its History

items.summary: Banks across several Indian states will stay closed on multiple days in November 2026 as Diwali, Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja, Bali Pratipada, Bhai Dooj and related regional festivals are observed. Closures fall on November 9, 10 and 11 depending on the state; for example, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and Sikkim close on the 10th. Branch-dependent transactions such as large cash deposits or cheque processing may be delayed, but ATMs, UPI, internet banking and mobile apps remain available.
items.title: Indian Banks Close for Diwali and Regional Festivals in November

items.summary: The Election Commission, stung by a public row over alleged internal dissent following an Indian Express report, issued on November 4 orders assigning Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Pawan Kumar Sharma to supervise Director General of IT Seema Khanna and deploying Prakash Rajpurohit to share responsibilities with Maneesh Garg. The moves follow commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu's objections to a July 28 order, which they say was never implemented after being recalled on July 30.
items.title: Election Commission Adds Oversight for Two Officials in Dissent Dispute

items.summary: One officer was killed and three others wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Lakewood, a suburb of Denver, Colorado, on Thursday evening. The shooting followed police responding to a report of a suspicious person trying to board a public bus around 6.30pm. Police spokesperson John Romero said the man opened fire as officers arrived; it was unclear whether this happened inside or near the bus.
items.title: Officer Killed and Three Wounded in Colorado Firefight

items.summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a retention option for ex-Agniveers, allowing those who fail to clear the merit cut after their initial four-year service under the Agnipath scheme to remain in Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) for two more years. The decision followed internal debates among CAPF chiefs and home ministry officials over how to assess merit without tests and where to post these highly trained soldiers, amid concerns about morale and integration with regular personnel who must pass three tests. Officials noted the quota increased from 10% to 50%, raising questions about direct induction versus competitive selection.
items.title: Cabinet Approves Agniveer Retention Option in CAPFs Amid Merit Debate

items.summary: President Donald Trump said he would review a 2022 law banning imports of Russian petroleum products but gave no timeline for change, reported ANI. He called the legislation possibly a bad law and agreed to look at it after being told by Congress signed it in 2022. The Treasury license covers only diesel until April 7, 2027, not all Russian oil.
items.title: Trump Reviews Law Banning Russian Petroleum Imports

items.summary: The Bhagya Lakshmi Temple at Charminar in Hyderabad opened round-the-clock from November 8 to 10 to distribute coins to devotees during Dhanteras celebrations. A large number of people turned up on Friday, with crowds swelling after the 7 am maharathi and continuing until midnight. Trustees Surya Prakash and Shashikala said coin distribution would begin at 7 pm on Sunday Diwali, with four entry and exit points provided for hassle-free darshan; police assisted in arrangements.
items.title: Bhagya Lakshmi Temple Opens Round-the-Clock for Dhanteras Coin Distribution

items.summary: A home tour of producer Anupriya Nagar's Juhu bungalow, featured on Curly Tales' YouTube channel, has drawn online attention amid speculation about her wealth. Though Hanuman Ansh reportedly grossed around Rs 420 crore worldwide, the article notes she was already affluent before its success.
items.title: Producer's Lavish Bungalow Sparks Wealth Speculation After Film Success

items.summary: A fire broke out early Friday at a four-storey commercial building selling mobile accessories inside Puri Plaza, 13 Block, Chain Wali Gali, Gaffar Market, Karol Bagh. Around 20-25 fire engines were rushed to the spot, and no loss of life or injuries was reported; only property damage occurred. Delhi Police received a PCR call at around 1:28 am. Overheating or overcharging of batteries appears to be a possible cause, with the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) team examining the building for other combustible material while further action awaits investigation findings.
items.title: Delhi Fire in Karol Bagh Building Draws Emergency Response

items.summary: Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, 2026, marking the start of Diwali. The page lists shubh muhurat times to buy gold, silver, vehicles, utensils and brooms in cities including New Delhi (6:02 PM–7:57 PM), Mumbai and Kolkata. Timings follow the New Delhi Panchang and may differ locally; even a small coin or utensil is said to invite blessings of Lakshmi, Dhanvantari and Kuber.
items.title: Dhanteras 2026 auspicious timings for buying gold, silver and utensils across India
